claims.title: N68 affine matrices give a one-query PIT for polynomially sparse rational division-free formulas
claims.interface: Formula tree in Q<x_1,...,x_n>, at most m vertices, total rational-leaf encoding length C, supplied unary support bound t, at most t distinct nonzero words, t <= poly(n+m+C); exact full M_(2t)(Q) response to one tuple query; no inverse gates.
claims.claim: With B=n+1, D=2t, and (A_i)_(a,b)=binom(b,a)B^a i^(b-a) for a<=b, f is zero iff f(A_1,...,A_n)=0.
claims.proof: The row v_D(z)=(1,z,...,z^(D-1)) satisfies v_D(z)A_i=v_D(Bz+i). Each word has an injective base-B code alpha(w), and v_D(1)f(A) contains the first 2t power moments of its at most t distinct integer codes. If f(A)=0, the first r moments vanish; the r-by-r Vandermonde matrix is nonsingular, forcing every coefficient to vanish.
claims.costs: Dense tuple output O(n t^3 log(n+1)) bits; deterministic construction polynomial in n,t. For formula size m and total constant bits C, response entries have O(C+m+m t log(n+1)) numerator/denominator bits and the full response has O(t^2(C+m+m t log(n+1))) bits. Naive formula evaluation uses O(m t^3) rational operations and conservative O(m t^3 H^2) bit operations for H=O(C+m+m t log(n+1)). The oracle computation and its full response are charged separately from tuple generation.
claims.domain_semantics: All queries are defined because the class is division-free.
claims.falsifier: A nonzero rational polynomial with at most t words evaluates to the zero matrix, equivalently a collision in the word codes or a failure of the stated Vandermonde argument.
claims.scope_limit: Does not cover general formulas with exponential support, succinct circuits with exponential degree, inverses, arbitrary coefficient fields, or general circuits. The N68 2t acquisition decoder is source-derived/unreviewed; this leaf proves the zero/nonzero consequence from its encoding.

claims.title: Formula size alone cannot be substituted for N68 sparsity
claims.interface: Division-free formula tree over Q with m vertices, evaluated through N68 with supplied sparsity t.
claims.claim: F_k=product_(j=1)^k (x_(2j-1)+x_(2j)) has 4k-1 tree vertices but exactly 2^k distinct words, so the N68 query dimension is 2^(k+1), not polynomial in formula size under t=support.
claims.costs: The full response has 4^(k+1) entries; the dense tuple has O(k 8^k log(k+1)) bits. Degree is only k, so the sparsity obstruction is independent of high degree.
claims.falsifier: A cancellation or collision among the 2^k distinct selected-variable words, or a different formula-tree count convention than the stated vertices-and-gates convention.
claims.scope_limit: Refutes only direct substitution t=poly(m) into N68. It is not a formula PIT lower bound.
claims.evidence: evidence/receipt.json; exact general proof in RESULT.txt

claims.title: N68's zero-test response does not preserve N51's defined-invertible rational interface
claims.claim: For n=1,t=2, the N68 A_1 has diagonal 1,2,4,8. The formula x_1-1 has nonzero singular response, while (x_1-2)^(-1) is undefined at that tuple but defined and nonzero at scalar x_1=0.
claims.costs: Constant-size exact rational witnesses. No approximation or bit-height issue.
claims.falsifier: A_1-2I is invertible or the rational expression is undefined/zero at scalar zero.
claims.scope_limit: Shows direct N68 tuple substitution cannot satisfy the N51 response/domain contract. A different rational-formula algorithm is not ruled out.

claims.title: A single tuple cannot replace N51's all-field strong-list interface
claims.claim: For any h integer matrix tuples, choose an eigenvalue lambda_j of the first matrix at tuple j over an algebraic closure. The rational formula (product_j(x_1-lambda_j))^(-1), of size 4h, is undefined at every list tuple and defined/invertible at a scalar avoiding all lambda_j. Therefore any universal defined-invertible list for size-s formulas over all coefficient fields requires h>=floor(s/4)+1.
claims.falsifier: A list with h<=floor(s/4) satisfies the stated all-field defined-invertible quantifier despite the eigenvalue denominator witness.
claims.scope_limit: An exact lower bound on the strong list interface, not a contradiction to polynomial-size N51 and not a general PIT query lower bound.

claims.title: N51 polynomial-bit output is not evidence of practical execution
claims.claim: The R06 source claims polynomial total output/time from unary n,B and preservation of inverse domains; the complete generator is explicitly unexecuted. Its n=B=1 large branch has K=3,453,153,708,034 and (K+1)^5 approximately 4.91e62 tuples.
claims.falsifier: A replay of the stated R06 parameter equations yields a different K/grid size, or an executed full promised-size generator contradicts its recorded unexecuted status.
claims.scope_limit: The R06 all-field theorem remains source-derived and not independently validated. The public 2026 rational-formula manuscript is a separate Q-scoped source.

overall_status: Internally proved scoped sparse-class theorem and exact interface counterexamples; finite replay passed. N68 source status is source-reported/source-derived as indicated. N51 R06 remains source-derived, unvalidated, and unexecuted. No novelty claim.
